chapter: Becoming a player; Rene, Bunk and Armstrong
title: Coming to Chicago at 15 and starting the trombone at 18
summary: He arrived at about 15, started to play at about 18 with good teachers, and joined the union in 1921.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well anyway, when we started talking about the first band you played with, you know, with Bernie Young and this guy. Buddy Young. Yeah and you played, you said it was mostly Ad-lib. Yeah Ad-lib. Now I want to ask you from the beginning one of the questions I want to ask. How old were you when you came to Chicago?
When I arrived in Chicago, I was 15, I was going on 16 years old.
And you hadn't started playing all that?
No, no I wasn't thinking about playing. And what gave you the idea of playing? My mother wanted me to play. Well she wanted you to play. Yeah, yeah.
And how old were you when you started?
When I started, I must have been about, maybe 18 years old. Yeah. Because I joined the union in 21.
So you started way later than like the early movement.
Oh yeah. I was behind Lee Carlton, I was behind Joe Rochelle, behind the Humphries.
Then you had good teachers. Yeah, I had good teachers.

You were lucky to have very good teachers. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Well the technology to me, I just stayed right in front of them all the time. I worried them, you know. Yeah. See Roy and his wife room with us. And I'd live for him in the kitchen. Well you had a good opportunity.
I'm going to go when I leave and practice a little bit, make my lift too flexible, you know. Because I'd like to do good tonight, you know. Yeah.
But anyway, so you started taking lessons when you were about 18 years old. And then when did you start playing music?
